A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Muses, and all 12 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains the Appendix mentioned in its text; the comparison covers all included material without assuming the contents of that unavailable supplement.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original generation comparisons, CLIP/VQA scores, human preferences, and component ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–6.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, with additional inanimate-object comparisons in Figure 7 and complexity-based module failure measurements in Table 3.

M1.justification: Both retain skeleton classification and LLM-guided assembly, skinning-based SLAT composition, and image-guided texture generation. The added explanation of interpolation in the existing 16³ latent space does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Beyond the existing creature examples incorporating animals, robots, and fictional characters, v2 Figure 7 evaluates two inanimate-object compositions: lamp base/aircraft aerofoil/folding fan and ship/kite/broom. This modestly extends the represented object domains.

E2.justification: The displayed comparisons retain DreamBeast, UNO+Trellis, Trellis-Text-to-3D, OmniPart, and the baseline labeled GaussianDreamer in figures/tables but called DreamGaussian [49] in prose. New Figure 7 uses the same comparator set; the naming inconsistency persists in both versions.

E3.justification: New Section 5.4 introduces failure-rate evaluation with 100 randomly sampled cases per complexity bin, defined using joint counts and counts of nodes with degree at least three. The existing 30-sample automatic evaluation, 10-example study with 60 volunteers, metrics, and generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4, Figure 8, and Table 3 add a focused robustness analysis of how skeleton classification and LLM assembly fail as skeleton complexity increases. The original five component ablations and qualitative failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new robustness experiment reports sampled-case counts and point failure rates, without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical values and rankings. New Table 3 reports easy/medium/hard failure rates of 5%/5%/8% for skeleton classification and 4%/7%/11% for LLM reasoning. Figure 7 adds qualitative results on two inanimate-object compositions; these are additional evaluations, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The SLAT definitions, graph rules, transformation operators, and weighting/generation equations (1)–(8) remain mathematically unchanged. The complexity thresholds define an evaluation protocol; no new theoretical derivation or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free, feed-forward fantasy-creature generation through skeleton-guided design, composition, and appearance generation, with superior fidelity and textual alignment.

C2.justification: v2 adds a semantic-latent explanation for easier gap bridging, explicitly discusses applicability to skeletonizable inanimate objects, and interprets the new failure rates as confirming robust scaling. The existing limitations concerning unsuccessful source generation and skeleton initialization remain.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same Trellis backbone, guidance scale 5.0, 25 sampling steps, RTX A6000 hardware, Puppeteer block depth 1, Qwen-plus, FLUX.1 Kontext, sub-minute generation claim, and project-page link. No implementation or resource-access revision is documented.

R1.justification: The same 75 reference entries and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Positioning against part-level assembly and creative-2D-to-3D approaches is unchanged; reference back-page numbers change with layout.

P1.justification: v2 locally condenses Section 5.2 and the Figure 6 caption, expands the interpolation explanation, adds a Robustness subsection and acknowledgements, and renumbers subsequent experimental subsections. The overall narrative and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned from a large creature montage into a compact rendered pedestal display, reshaping the opening-page layout. v2 also adds the inanimate-object comparison grid, skeleton-complexity illustration, and failure-rate table, relocates Tables 1–2, and reorganizes surrounding text and figures. The original application and failure figures remain as Figures 9–10.

improvement.justification: The new inanimate-object comparisons and complexity-based failure measurements provide useful evidence about applicability and reliability that v1 lacked, while preserving the established method and results. The gain is limited: the domain extension has only two illustrated cases, and the robustness study lacks explicit failure criteria and uncertainty estimates, weakening its claim of confirmed robust scaling.
